claim: A holdout test reserves a baseline experience so you can measure whether a new system beats the status quo — not only which variant won among tested arms.
definition: A holdout is a reserved share of traffic kept on the baseline experience while the experimental system (e.g. multi-variant predictive allocation) runs on the rest. Lift is measured against the holdout, not only pairwise A/B winners.
caveats: Relative winners inside a closed race do not prove the program beat status quo.
